To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the DSM-IV symptom criteria were useful in differentiating between pain-related and non pain-related symptoms of analgesic dependence among SCD patients, and that pain-related symptoms were more prevalent than non-pain-related ones.

pain-related and not pain-related DSM-IV symptoms were common among SCD patients and that the frequency of dependence on analgesics was substantially higher when pain-related symptoms were assessed than when they were excluded.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the social construction of analgesic dependence among patients with SCD.
how patients' perceptions of dependence on analgesics may affect their pain management and treatment in hospital.
the implications of the DSM-IV diagnostic criteria for substance dependence in relation to the assessment of dependence in SCD patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the findings indicate the presence of a substantial proportion of patients with SCD with symptoms of dependence on analgesic drugs and that this dependence is largely pain-related.

the findings suggest that patients with SCD may be vulnerable to perceptions of analgesic dependence, but this does not necessarily indicate that they have a substance abuse problem or that analgesic treatment for SCD should be restricted.
there is a need for a better understanding of the relationship of pain and dependence in SCD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the pain management needs to be improved for patients with Sickle Cell Disease.

the DSM-IV substance dependence criteria may need revision to take into account pain-related analgesic use, which is common in SCD and in other painful conditions, such as chronic back pain and rheumatoid arthritis.
pain-related dependence on analgesics in SCD should not be interpreted as evidence of substance dependence.
The main takeaway from our work is that
pain-related symptoms of dependence are common in SCD.
pain-related symptoms of substance abuse and dependence are common in SCD and are not a reliable marker of dependence on prescribed analagesia.
pain management is an important aspect of the care of patients with sickle disease and that the perception of dependence on prescribed opioids is common in these patients.
